It closes the four count_only tools the TASK-115 report left open, by pairing each write with a content-level read-back IN THE SAME RUN: editor_add_gridmap <- editor_get_scene_tree (the created GridMap node is listed), editor_set_node_script_batch <- editor_execute_gdscript (Node.get_script().resource_path, the witness TASK-115 proved works where editor_get_node_properties -32001s on 'script'), editor_connect_signal <- editor_list_signal_connections (the connection table itself), and running_game_find_node_when_available <- its own answer, because it is a READ-verb tool whose successful payload IS the measurement ({"found":true,...}). Project: _exercises/ex_grid (it owns assets/meshlib.tres AND a playable main.tscn, so one run serves both endpoints). No save-scene call: every editor write stays in memory, the game endpoint reads main.tscn from disk untouched.
